Subject: Order Form questions: invoicing entity & tax residency

Hi Priya,

Thanks for sending the draft order form earlier today. A couple of items finance flagged that we need clarified before we can proceed to countersign:

- Invoicing entity: Solace prefers invoices addressed to Solace US Holdings, Inc. (parent) rather than the local European affiliate. Will Redwood be able to invoice the US entity for the full committed amount?
- Tax residency / VAT: our EU subsidiary says that if the US parent is invoiced, they may need a reverse-charge notation on the invoice and a VAT certificate on file. Can Redwood accept this flow?
- Net terms: Finance is requesting Net 45 instead of Net 30 for this contract. Is that acceptable?
- Minimum commit language: we'd like the first-tranche commitment to be split into two installments (60% on signature, 40% 90 days later) rather than a single upfront payment — any flexibility?

I've attached our copy of the draft (Solace_OrderForm_Draft.pdf) with highlighting on the invoicing and tax sections.

Can we get a short note back today with which of the above Redwood can accept and what evidence (tax docs, PO routing info) we'll need to provide? We're hoping to keep the timeline for signature this month.

Best,

Ben / Kim — looping you in on Solace's asks (see email pasted below). They want: invoice to US parent, a possible reverse-charge VAT note if we do that, Net 45, and a split first tranche.

Quick summary of Redwood position / questions for commercial/legal:
- Invoicing entity: We can invoice the US parent but need to confirm how Accounting will route revenue and whether we accept remittance to a different legal entity. Ben — can you confirm revenue recognition implications and whether Finance is okay receiving a US-invoice for services delivered to an EU affiliate?
- Tax evidence: If we invoice the US parent and the EU affiliate claims reverse-charge, we'll need a VAT registration / certificate from the EU entity and an explicit reverse-charge line on the invoice. Kim — is that acceptable from a risk/compliance perspective? Any required wording?
- Net terms: We can consider Net 45 for this customer at the pilot tier; propose adding a 1.5% early-payment credit for Net 15 to protect cash flow. Thoughts?
- Minimum commit / phasing: Suggested commercial compromise: 60% upfront (signature), 20% at 90 days, 20% at 180 days. If accepted, we should reflect as a three-line billing schedule on the order form and show proration in the billing matrix.

I've attached a proposed billing matrix and a redline we started (proposed_billing_matrix.xlsx, redline_orderform.docx). Please review and provide: (1) legal redline needed for tax language, (2) finance sign-off on invoicing to US parent, (3) whether the staircase commit above is acceptable.

If we can close these items this morning I will send a single consolidated reply to Emily with our final ask and a next-step (DocuSign timeline).

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Priya / Kim / Marissa — quick commercial inputs from my side:

- Revenue / invoicing: Finance is generally OK invoicing the US parent but needs a signed Billing Recommendation (we'll formalize in the billing matrix). We will record revenue to the US entity and will require Solace to sign a one-line routing statement confirming payment to Solace US Holdings. If legal wants the invoice to reference the underlying EU entity, we can add a "served-to" line.

- Minimum commit / split: The 60 / 20 / 20 split Priya suggested looks reasonable. I recommend we add language that the remaining tranches become due regardless of usage but are eligible for pro-rata credit if the customer downgrades services within 60 days of the tranche date.

- Net terms: Net 45 is acceptable for this deal tier. To mitigate cash impact, propose a 1% early pay credit for payment within 10 days, 1.5% for payment within 15 days.

- Tax evidence: For reverse-charge we will require Solace's EU VAT registration number and a signed confirmation that the EU affiliate will self-account for VAT. If Solace cannot provide the VAT cert, we will invoice with VAT applied to the EU invoice path.

Attaching my suggested commit schedule with amounts by tranche (commit_schedule_v1.xlsx). If Kim approves legal language, I can fold into the final order form and routing statement.

Priya / Ben — legal checklist and redline pointers below (high level):

1) Invoicing entity and tax language
- We can accept invoicing the US parent as proposed, but we must add a clause that Redwood's invoice to the US entity is "sufficient for payment" and that Solace will provide supporting tax documentation for any reverse-charge treatment.
- Insert the following: "Customer shall provide (i) the EU affiliate's VAT registration number and (ii) a written confirmation of intent to self-account for VAT (reverse charge) prior to Redwood issuing an invoice without VAT. Absent such evidence, applicable VAT will be applied to the invoice."

2) Tax indemnity / cap
- Limit Redwood's indemnity for taxes to material misrepresentations and require the customer to indemnify Redwood for taxes arising from Customer's incorrect tax residency statements. Add a $250k cap for the indemnity clause for order-form level.

3) Invoice remittance and PO flow
- Add a required PO number field on the invoice and routing statement that must be included for accounts-payable processing. Also add a clause that any change to invoicing entity after countersign requires 30 days' notice.

4) Billing schedule language
- Add explicit non-refundable designation for the upfront tranche and clarify crediting rules for subsequent tranches (Ben's pro-rata credit language OK; legal will add one-line exception for force majeure).

5) Evidence and audit
- Request the VAT certificate and any tax-residency declarations to be uploaded to our secure shared Drive before the first invoice. We'll include a 30-day cure period for missing docs.

I've attached a redlined order form with the proposed language (orderform_legal_redline.docx). Once Priya confirms commercial amounts, I'll finalize redlines and prepare the DocuSign packet.

Kimberly Park
